```python
from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

def find_best_coloring(n):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()

    # Variables for each diagonal being green or red (0 or 1)
    diagonals = {}
    for i in range(1, n+1):
        for j in range(i+1, n+1):
            if abs(j-i) > 1 and abs(j-i) != n-1:  # Diagonals, not sides or opposite vertices
                diagonals[(i,j)] = model.NewBoolVar(f'diag_{i}_{j}')

    # Constraints: exactly n-3 green and n-3 red diagonals
    model.Add(sum(diagonals[d] for d in diagonals) == n-3)
    model.Add(sum(1-diagonals[d] for d in diagonals) == n-3)

    # No two diagonals of the same color intersect inside M
    for (i1, j1) in diagonals:
        for (i2, j2) in diagonals:
            if i1 < i2 and j1 > j2:  # Check for intersection
                model.Add(diagonals[(i1,j1)] + diagonals[(i2,j2)] <= 1)
                model.Add((1-diagonals[(i1,j1)]) + (1-diagonals[(i2,j2)]) <= 1)

    # Solve the model
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    status = solver.Solve(model)
    
    if status == cp_model.OPTIMAL or status == cp_model.FEASIBLE:
        green_diags = [(i, j) for (i, j) in diagonals if solver.Value(diagonals[(i,j)]) == 1]
        red_diags = [(i, j) for (i, j) in diagonals if solver.Value(diagonals[(i,j)]) == 0]
        return green_diags, red_diags
    else:
        return None, None

# Find the best coloring for a 15-gon
green_diagonals, red_diagonals = find_best_coloring(15)

# Format the result
result = f"{str(tuple(green_diagonals))}, {str(tuple(red_diagonals))}"
print(result)
```
